reader.requirement: At --std 85 an elementary report entry whose SUM clause repeats the SUM phrase (SUM a UPON d1 SUM b UPON d2 ...) must establish exactly one sum counter, into which every phrase's addends accumulate under its own UPON filter, and the entry's data-name must name that one counter.

edition-consulted.switches: SumCounterDigits(pic, Edition.DialectLevel): the counter's size by the 1985 GR1 table (18-digit alphanumeric cap) versus later editions; the size of the one counter, not how many

reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf09_09 has one SUM phrase per entry; an entry with several SUM phrases is not exercised

probes.printed: S-MUL (SUM W-A UPON DET1 SUM W-B UPON DET2) 21, 3, 4; S-X (SUM S-MUL S-MUL) 42
probes.expected: one counter: W-A=1 on DET1 plus W-B=20 on DET2 = 21; a crossfoot of the name reads that single counter (2*21)

probes.printed: COBOL1559 'writes its SUM clause in more than one piece' and COBOL2423 'the clause ... is written 2 times' for SUM W-A UPON DET1 COLUMN 11 SUM W-B UPON DET2
probes.expected: the §1985:XIII.3.9.2 Format 3 entry has one SUM clause slot, so a second SUM clause separated by another clause is not a legal form; the repeated phrase inside one clause is

reader.notes: BindSumClause makes one ReportSumModel per entry with one ReportSumTerm per SUM phrase; the emitter registers one AddSum and an AddSumTerm per phrase, so the runtime holds one SumEntry. The diagnostics for a split clause cite §2023 at --std 85 (a wording point outside this rule).

refuter.evidence: sum3a-001: S-PH SUM W-A SUM W-A SUM W-B, three SUM phrases in one entry, accumulated into one counter (12, 24, 36). A Procedure Division DISPLAY S-PH by the entry's data-name after the first GENERATE read that one counter ('S-PH +012'), and a rolled SUM S-PH S-PH S-PH in CF FINAL read it as one addend (216). GR5 ('the data-name is the name of the sum counter') is honoured at 85 through an 85-only lookup arm the reader did not list (see edition-sites-missed). The reader's sum2 covered the refusal of a second SUM clause split by another clause. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.19.4 GR3  (3.19.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.19.4 GR5  (3.19.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5'.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/ReportSectionBinder.cs#SumCounterOperand85: DialectLevel < 2002 resolves a written reference to the one sum counter an entry establishes (an ambiguity diagnostic when two entries share the name); at 2002+ it returns null and the ordinary lookup answers
